checks.description: The real orchestrator container reports healthy.
Live connector writes are disabled by default while synthetic writes are enabled.
A Gmail send request creates a task-scoped owner approval.
A Calendar create-event request creates a task-scoped owner approval.
A GitHub create-issue request creates a task-scoped owner approval.
Execution before owner approval is rejected.
All connector write approvals are visible in the existing approval queue.
Approved Gmail synthetic execution completes and persists a receipt reference.
Approved Calendar synthetic execution completes and persists a receipt reference.
Approved GitHub synthetic execution completes and persists a receipt reference.
Repeating an idempotency key reuses the original action and approval.
Re-executing an already completed action does not create a second mutation receipt.
Connector action history retains completed synthetic receipts and timestamps.
Each action links provider, kind, summary, task, approval and action type for review.
Even after approval, a LIVE mutation attempt is rejected while live writes are disabled.
Evidence explicitly distinguishes synthetic hosted writes from live provider mutation, production autonomy and physical-PC validation.
